title: Jerry Fielding and his first steady TV show, The Life of Riley
summary: He started studio work with Fielding's orchestra, first on the William Bendix show, scoring background music.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: ...and Maxwell. Three saxophones and a rhythm section. It was just a sextet. But it was some hard swing, and that was enjoyment for me. Another thing, "You're Part Of Me"; that's a tune of mine I wrote, and Felicia Sanders wrote... Do you remember her?

She wrote the lyric to that. Because during that same period is when I was working with the Jerry Fielding Orchestra, and getting my feet wet in the studios. My first steady show was The Life Of Riley.
I can't remember how much music was on The Life Of Riley.
Just background music. However, Jerry just wrote beautifully for whatever he did. It was a thing featuring William Bendix; it was his show.
I remember the show very vaguely, but...
Well, you must have been a child when that was...
Thank you, Red. Thank you. No. But I don't remember it musically; I just remember William Bendix.
Well, the music was incidental, you know, open door music and...knock-knock, open the door. And it was background music. But that was my first steady TV show.
What did you work after that?
